neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were the husband and relatives of the husband of the deceased, were involved in a case where the deceased committed suicide. The deceased was married to one of the accused, and after the marriage, she was subjected to mental torture and harassment due to insufficient dowry. The deceased's father received a call informing him of the incident and arrived at the scene. The police registered a complaint against the accused, and the accused were arrested. During the trial, several witnesses testified about the mental torture and harassment the deceased faced. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 304-B and 498-A of the IPC. The High Court upheld the conviction, and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, affirming the conviction.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased died by committing suicide within seven years of her marriage and that four witnesses proved that cruelty was meted out to the deceased immediately before her death, leading to the presumption that the suicide was abetted by the accused.

quotes.text: The prosecution argued that the deceased died by committing suicide within seven years of her marriage and that four witnesses proved that cruelty was meted out to the deceased immediately before her death, leading to the presumption that the suicide was abetted by the accused.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to substantiate the guilt of the accused under Sections 304-B and 306 of the IPC, and that the evidence of relatives and friends of the deceased was not reliable and could not be solely relied upon.

quotes.text: The counsel for the appellants contended that the prosecution has failed to substantiate the guilt of the appellants under Sections 306 and 3048 of IPC.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that Sections 304-B and 498-A of the IPC are not mutually inclusive, and that a presumption under Section 113-A of the Evidence Act can be raised if certain foundational facts are established and the event occurred within seven years of marriage.

quotes.text: Section 304-B and Section 498A of IPC are not mutually inclusive. If an accused is acquitted under one section, it does not mean that the accused cannot be convicted under another section.
